title: BUG: DataFrame.query with `@` reference to a class attribute
body:
- [x] closes #48694

`df.query("x == @A.a")` and `df.eval("x == @A.a")` raise `UndefinedVariableError` when `A` is a class. #47273 marks a name as non-local when its value in scope is a type, so that a column named `Timestamp` is found instead of `pandas.Timestamp`. That check also ran for names written with `@`, so `@A` was looked up in the columns. It now only applies to names without `@`.

The same change was proposed by @jbrockmendel in #65945, which he closed on 2026-06-27 along with a number of his other open PRs, without review. This PR carries it forward, with the test extended to cover `eval` and both engines.

The new test covers `query` and `eval` with both engines, and fails without the fix. `pandas/tests/computation` and `pandas/tests/frame/test_query_eval.py` pass, apart from `test_scalar_unary[numexpr-pandas]`, which also fails on main for me (a `~bool` DeprecationWarning on Python 3.12).
